mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the GDP contraction is accompanied by a simultaneous stock rally.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 6% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or inflation does not rise concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the decline is accompanied by a surge in consumer demand proxies.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in HOUST and a decrease in RSAFS over two months signals a shift from speculative investment to real demand, which historically precedes a stabilization phase and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND RSAFS < previous month for two months
regime_hint: transition from speculative to real economy
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the pattern is not followed by a sustained rally.

mechanism_narrative: A positive co-movement between PAYEMS and UNRATE above their respective 3-month averages for three months indicates synchronized labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 3-mo avg AND UNRATE > 3-mo avg for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or wage growth does not accelerate.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in CPIAUCSL below 1.5% for two consecutive months, combined with stable FEDFUNDS, signals disinflation without rate hikes, which historically supports risk asset appreciation and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS unchanged
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or inflation expectations rise sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in GDPC1 above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a robust demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth is not accompanied by earnings growth.
